---
# Positive control for the float branch of the overflow detector. Not an
# example: this poster exists to overflow, and to overflow in one specific
# way. It lives outside examples/ for that reason, and .quartoignore keeps it
# out of the shipped extension. template.qmd is the matching negative control
# — it carries a bottom-pinned float and must stay quiet.
#
# The failure it reproduces: a bottom-pinned `.full-width` float shortens the
# columns region, but the body sits in a FIXED-height grid row, and Typst does
# not clip a block that outgrows its row. Column text that runs past the
# shortened region therefore keeps drawing, straight under the float, which is
# painted on top of it. The result is one page, with the lost text sitting
# well above the page bottom — so a guard that compares against the page edge
# sees nothing wrong. That is exactly how a heading and a paragraph went
# missing from template.qmd once already.
#
# One column, so every filler paragraph lands in the single column the float
# shortens. The float is deliberately tall: the guard fires when the body ends
# inside the float's span, and a tall float widens that window well past the
# difference between one font stack's line metrics and another's. Measured on
# this fixture, everything from 9 filler paragraphs upward fires and nothing
# up to 28 crosses into the other branch; it carries 13, so a font with wider
# metrics than the one this was tuned on only pushes it further inside.
title: "Overflow guard fixture: content under a bottom float"
format:
  sciposter-typst:
    poster:
      size: a2
      columns: 1
---

# Filler

Creel surveys estimate angler effort, catch, harvest, and exploitation. The
analysis is often assembled from spreadsheets, borrowed scripts, and
disconnected software, so assumptions are hard to document and uncertainty is
hard to carry forward.

Standard data structures and validation make assumptions visible.
Design-based estimation keeps sampling structure attached to the reported
number. Comparisons hold up across systems, seasons, designs, and analysts.

Each design brings its own estimator: stratified effort from periodic counts,
Horvitz-Thompson expansion of PPS site selection, count imputation for
cameras, and calibrated open-hours scaling for aerial overflights.

The package automates the repeatable computation; survey objectives, design
choices, and management decisions remain human work. Effort, CPUE, harvest,
release, and exploitation all come back with variance attached.

# This heading and the text under it are drawn behind the float

Biologists work in creel vocabulary — dates, strata, counts, interviews,
effort, catch, lengths, schedules — while the package handles design-based
inference. None of this paragraph is visible in the rendered poster.

::: {.full-width position="bottom"}
::: {.takeaway label="Bottom float"}
A bottom-pinned float is painted over whatever outgrew the columns region.
It is deliberately tall: the guard fires when the body ends inside the
float's span, and a taller float widens that window past the difference
between one font's line metrics and another's.
:::
:::
